jobs.title: Housing Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: Housing Program Coordinator
SUPERVISOR: WSAG Executive Director
RESPONSIBLE TO: WSAG Governing Board

GOAL:
In collaboration with the WSAG team, coordinate emergency housing through direct case management and outreach.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Computer literacy and ability to use a spreadsheet to track data such as daily phone calls, waitlists, room use, and timesheets
Answer company-assigned telephone during posted hours of operation
Monitor social media inquiries
Outreach and attendance to local organizations and events directly supporting unhoused and inadequately housed people in WSAG service area
Intake and placement of clients for both short and longer-term stays
Room check before and after a client is housed
Connect to resources using brochures and pamphlets 

Longer-term Clients (10+ days)

Comprehensive intake and needs assessment within 72 hours of enrollment (including MH screening)
Connect with Long Valley Health regarding support with recipients with behavioral health needs
Create and monitor individualized Stabilization Plan/s
Initiate Crisis and Safety Plans
Initiate daily check-ins with clients, and weekly in-person or virtual case management meetings
Manage housing search assistance
Perform landlord outreach and engagement
Data collection and administration of applications and submissions support
Rental history problem-solving
Coordination of move-in assistance
Referrals to County Behavioral Health and community providers
Warm handoffs to treatment providers
Coordination of appointments and follow-up
Screening for eligibility (CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, SSI/SSDI, General Assistance)
Application assistance

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:

At least three years of direct experience with the unhoused population, housing, and at least one year of experience connecting people with resources such as NGOs and local governments. Degree or certification in Human Services or Behavioral Health preferred.
Pass background check and drug test
Ability to communicate effectively and clearly (both written and oral communication) 
Must be able to interact effectively with other employees in all levels of the organization as well as with the general public.

jobs.title: SART Program Coordinator RN
jobs.description:
*Job Summary and Responsibilities*

As our SART Program Coordinator RN, you will lead and drive the operations of the Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) program serving our Santa Barbara County community. You will set the administrative direction of the program while remaining clinically engaged—participating in the examiner call rotation to care for acute adult, adolescent, and pediatric patients in the Emergency Department. As a central liaison and dedicated patient/victim advocate, you will sustain compassionate, continuous communication with physicians, patients, families, community agencies, and county partners.

Every day, you will deliver comprehensive, trauma-informed acute examinations and precise case management grounded in your scope of licensure and regulatory protocols. You will oversee the meticulous, timely collection and preservation of forensic evidence—maintaining strict chain of custody—for law enforcement and future judicial proceedings, and you will extend your impact beyond the exam room by providing expert witness testimony in court. You will develop and refine program protocols, evaluate outcomes, review SANE charts and evidentiary documentation, and partner with the District Attorney’s SART Coordinator and Santa Barbara County SART Coalition to strengthen coordinated survivor care.

To be successful in this role, you will draw on substantial specialized knowledge, clinical judgment, and advanced skill rooted in the biological, physiological, behavioral, and sociological sciences. You will apply critical thinking to integrate established standards, community resources, and patient data into rapid, accurate care decisions. Your ability to pair clinical expertise with organizational leadership will show up in the way you recruit, onboard, train, and validate the competency of Sexual Assault Nurse Examiners; facilitate quarterly SART education; manage site operations, supplies, and SART billing with the DA’s office; and support annual reporting, grant development, and community prevention efforts.

What You Bring

BSN and active RN licensure, with three years of staff nursing experience
Current BLS
SANE-A and/or SANE-P certification and prior SANE training (preferred)
Bilingual skills (preferred)
Knowledge of rape trauma theory, medico-legal forensic standards, evidence collection, and courtroom testimony protocols

Join us in a role where clinical excellence and advocacy meet—ensuring justice, dignity, and healing for survivors across our community.

*Job Requirements**Required*

Bachelors Of Science in Nursing - BSN
Three years of staff nursing work experience that demonstrates attainment of the requisite job knowledge skills/abilities
Registered Nurse: CA (RN:CA)
Basic Life Support - CPR (BLS-CPR)

*Preferred*

Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner Adult (SANE-A)
Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner Pediatric (SANE-P)

Where You'll Work

Founded in 1940, Dignity Health - Marian Regional Medical Center is a 191-bed, acute care, nonprofit hospital located in Santa Maria, California. Serving over 250,000 patients annually, the hospital offers a full complement of services including Level II Trauma Center, Level III NICU, cancer care, orthopedics, and stroke care. Additionally, Marian Regional Medical Center has been recognized as an LGBTQ+ Healthcare Equality High Performer by the Human Rights Campaign Foundation. It is a Joint Commission-certified Primary Stroke Center, and the only healthcare facility on the Central Coast to offer ECMO.

[One Community. One Mission. One California ](https://youtu.be/RrPuiSnALJY?si=pvQgPZ6ZWZM60TPV)

$57.02 - $86.80 /hour

jobs.title: PT Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Community Health Worker is responsible for spreading awareness about CoH, assisting in providing high quality programs, leading the effort to increase access to financial assistance, and ensuring financial compliance. You must fully support Cradle of Hope’s mission, work within established guidelines and policies, and be responsible for specific projects as assigned.

Schedule & Benefits

This is a part time position (20 hrs/wk). Pay Rate: $23/hour, paid holidays, paid time off: 3 weeks (12 days). Work Schedule: Monday – Thursday from 9:30 – 3:00 (½ hour unpaid lunch break) and then enjoy a long weekend.

Qualifications

Cradle of Hope is a pro-life agency. CoH’s mission is to encourage life by providing financial aid to women and babies in crisis, especially those women who might not choose life because of financial pressures. Must fully support Cradle of Hope’s mission and programs; able to positively interact with others; able to multi-task, be flexible, problem solve, and pay attention to detail; proficient using Microsoft Word and Excel; able to work as part of a team and independently; a Bachelor’s Degree and 2 years of experience training adults (in a classroom setting, community education environment, or other venue providing instruction to others or working with pregnant women/families in crisis) is required. Must have a valid driver’s license and dependable transportation.

Duties And Responsibilities

Ensures delivery and implementation of CoH’s Financial Assistance program in accordance with the mission, goals, and policies of CoH.
Develops an outreach strategy to spread awareness about CoH. Attends and assists with fundraising events and CoH initiatives.
Develops an outreach strategy to increase the number of clients receiving financial assistance and the number of CoH partnering agencies submitting financial assistance applications.
Processes financial assistance applications. Ensures that CoH operates within budgetary and financial guidelines. Collaborates with the Executive Director to discuss proposed budgetary deviations or alterations.
Screens clients for financial assistance eligibility and completes in-person financial assistance applications with clients and follow-up evaluations.
Processes and maintains all financial assistance paperwork, releases, and reports.
Conducts financial assistance training to new and existing partnering agencies and provide on-going training/support as needed (including site visits when needed). Add financial assistance sites as needed. Maintain and develop relationships with social workers, healthcare personnel, and trained volunteers working at partnering agencies.
Provide referrals to those calling CoH for help. You are responsible for listening to the needs of the caller, navigating resources available, and providing information that aligns with the caller’s unique circumstances.
Increase the number of individuals/agencies donating baby items to CoH. Coordinates a steady flow of donations for baby shower basket items and writes thank you letters to those donating. Monitors the inventory of all baby supplies and cribs.
Assists in daily operations such as processing crib applications, safe sleep classes, completing office documentation, and responding to calls.
Become familiar with all CoH social media and ensure that it is updated and accurate.
Attends and participates in staff meetings. Participates in the Strategic Planning of CoH.
Presents any funding ideas you may have to ensure the continuous delivery of services.

Work Location: In person

Please email cover letter and resume to Darlene Kopesky at: dkopesky@cradleofhope.org

At Monarch Communities, we value compassion, innovation, and community. Our team is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of our residents and fostering a collaborative and supportive work environment.

Job Description

The Caregiver will report to Health & Wellness Director. The Caregiver is a non-exempt, hourly position.

Job Overview - Full-time and Part-time and PRN

Salary Range: $19.00 - $23.00 Hourly

Assists residents in all aspects of their daily life as indicated in the resident’s care plan, including personal care, food service, housekeeping, laundry, behavior management, socialization, and activities.

Responsibilities and Duties

Provide resident care to residents that include bathing, dressing, toileting, and feeding, as outlined in their care plan
Maintain the safety, comfort, dignity, and confidentiality of all residents
Escort residents to meals and activities
Ensures all assigned residents are clean, neatly dressed and groomed, safe, and fed during assigned shifts
Document all services provided to your assigned residents during your shift
Report any change of condition in a resident immediately to your supervisor

Certified Nursing Assistant
High School Diploma
Knowledge and experience in working with the elderly population, preferred dementia experience

While performing the duties of this job, the associate is often required to stand, walk, sit, use fine and gross motor skills, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, hear, and smell.
An individual in this position will be required to lift or carry weight in up to 50 lbs. Intermittent physical activity includes lifting and supporting residents. The associate must use proper body mechanics.
